Main Water Line Repair Cost: What to Expect and Why

By SRQ Leak Pros Editorial · Published November 5, 2026 · Updated November 5, 2026 · 7 min read

Short answer: Angi's national data puts the average main water line repair cost at about $1,025, with most jobs between about $354 and $1,696. Plumbers charge about $45 to $200 an hour in that data. Your water line repair cost rises with depth, concrete or pavers over the pipe, leak detection time and permit needs.

A leak in your main water line usually means a bill you didn't plan for. The good news is that a repair often costs far less than a full replacement. If your line is leaking, SRQ Leak Pros can connect you with a local provider for water service line repair in Sarasota who can price your job.

These are national figures from one source, Angi, updated December 2024. Use them to judge quotes, not as a price list.

How much does main water line repair cost?

Angi's data puts the average at about $1,025. Most homeowners pay between about $354 and $1,696. That covers a typical repair on the line from the meter to the house: finding the leak, opening the ground and fixing a section of pipe.

ItemAngi national figure
Average repairAbout $1,025
Typical rangeAbout $354 to $1,696
Plumber laborAbout $45 to $200 per hour
Full replacement, for comparisonAbout $1,710 average; about $50 to $250 per linear foot

What changes your water line repair cost?

  • Finding the leak. A pinpointed leak means one small hole. A hunt across the yard takes longer.
  • Depth. Deeper pipe means more digging.
  • What sits on top. Lawn is cheap to restore. Concrete, pavers and pools are not.
  • Pipe material. Some older pipe needs special fittings or a longer section replaced.
  • Access. Fences, trees and tight side yards slow the work.
  • Permits. Some repairs need a permit and inspection.
  • Urgency. After-hours or rush work can cost more.
  • Restoration. Sod, sprinkler repair and concrete patching may be extra.

Repair vs. replacement: which costs less?

A single repair costs less today. A replacement can cost less over time if the line keeps failing.

SituationUsually better
First leak in a sound lineRepair
Second or third leak in a few yearsReplacement quote
Polybutylene or galvanized lineReplacement
Line under a driveway or poolCompare repair, bore and reroute
Low pressure plus leaksReplacement

See the water line replacement cost guide for full replacement figures.

What's included in a water line repair quote?

A clear quote lists each step:

  1. Leak detection. How the leak will be found and confirmed.
  2. Locates. The Sunshine 811 call so other utilities get marked.
  3. Excavation. Size and depth of the hole.
  4. Repair. Pipe type, fittings and length replaced.
  5. Testing. A pressure test before backfill.
  6. Backfill and restoration. Soil, sod, concrete or pavers.
  7. Permit and inspection. If needed.

Ask what isn't included. Restoration is the most common surprise.

Hidden costs to ask about

  • Water damage cleanup, if the leak reached the house
  • A new main shut-off valve while the line is open
  • Sprinkler lines cut during digging
  • Concrete or paver matching
  • A second visit if the first repair fails

Does insurance pay for main water line repair?

Often not for the pipe itself. Many homeowners policies treat a worn service line as wear and tear. Some sell a separate service line endorsement. Some utilities and third parties offer service line plans. Read the terms closely. This is general information, not insurance advice.

Florida rules that affect the price

Florida requires a call to Sunshine 811 at least two full business days before digging. Florida also places repair of the water line from the meter to the building within a plumbing contractor's scope under § 489.105(3)(m). Hire a licensed plumbing contractor and check the license on the DBPR site.

If the leak sits between the street and the meter, it may be the utility's to fix. Sarasota County's leak FAQ says its staff decide whether each reported leak is the county's or the customer's. That can save you the whole bill, so call the utility first.

Sarasota factors that move the price

Sarasota's sandy soil is quick to dig, which can help the labor side. A high water table near the coast can fill holes with water and slow the repair. Many homes have pavers, pools and dense landscaping over the line, which raises restoration costs. Summer storms can also delay outdoor work.

How to keep your repair bill down

  • Find the meter and main shut-off before you need them.
  • Call the utility first to rule out a street-side leak.
  • Ask for leak detection before any digging.
  • Get two written quotes for larger jobs.
  • Ask whether a bore or reroute would save restoration costs.

Water line repair cost by type of problem

Angi's data also breaks repair costs down by the kind of job.

Repair typeAngi rangeAngi average
Replacing a line sectionAbout $100 to $200 per linear footAbout $150 per foot
Corroded water lineAbout $600 to $5,000About $2,800
Valve repairAbout $150 to $300About $225
Overall low to high endAbout $150 to $3,960About $1,025

A valve repair near the meter or the house is often the cheapest job. A corroded line is often a sign that the whole run is near the end of its life.

Does pipe material change the cost?

Yes, mostly through labor and fittings. Angi lists the material itself at a small share of the bill. Its per-foot pipe costs run about $0.40 to $2 for PEX, about $0.50 to $1 for CPVC, about $2 to $5 for polyethylene and about $2 to $8 for copper. Labor, digging and restoration make up most of the price. Older pipe like polybutylene or galvanized steel may need transition fittings or a longer section replaced, because the old pipe near the leak is often weak too.

Landscaping, concrete and permit costs

Restoration can cost more than the repair. Angi puts landscaping repair after a water main job at about $300 to $16,000, depending on how much was damaged and what you choose to upgrade. It notes most building permits cost about $50 to $300. Ask each bidder:

  • Is sod or seed included, or only backfill?
  • Who repairs sprinkler lines cut during the dig?
  • Will concrete be patched or replaced to the nearest joint?
  • Are pavers lifted and relaid by the same crew?
  • Is the permit fee in the price?

Trenched vs. trenchless repair costs

Angi describes trenchless repair as a method that needs only up to two small holes. It says trenchless work is generally more time- and cost-effective than an open trench. For a short repair under lawn, a small open hole is often cheapest. For a line under a driveway or pool deck, a trenchless bore or reroute can save on restoration. Our guide to trenchless water line replacement explains the methods.

How to budget for a main water line repair

  1. Get the leak pinpointed first. Detection keeps the dig small.
  2. Ask for a range, not just a number. Unknown depth or pipe condition can change the price.
  3. Plan for restoration. Set aside money for sod, concrete or pavers.
  4. Ask about the whole line. If the pipe is old, get a replacement price too.
  5. Check payment terms. Ask when deposits and final payments are due.

Local note: long service lines on North Port lots can add to locating time. In Siesta Key, tight lots and a high water table can complicate a dig. Paver drives in Lakewood Ranch can often be lifted and relaid.

Related reading: confirm who is responsible for the water line from the street to the house. If the leak is under concrete, see water leak under the driveway. To check first, read the signs of a water service line leak.

When should you call a water line professional?

Call a pro when:

  • Your meter moves with all water off
  • You see a wet strip between the meter and the house
  • Water pressure drops suddenly
  • You want a repair and a replacement price side by side

Frequently asked questions

How long does a main water line repair take?

Many repairs take a few hours once the leak is found. Locates, permits and restoration can add days.

Can I repair a main water line myself?

Florida treats service line repair as plumbing contractor work. A pro also handles locates, testing and permits.

Is a water line repair cheaper than replacement?

Usually, for one leak. If the line keeps failing, replacement may cost less over time.

Why did my water line repair quote seem high?

Depth, concrete, pavers, restoration and detection time often drive the price. Ask for a line-by-line quote.
